chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Ayyūb ibn al-Ḥurr, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is affected by flowing blood. He said: “He performs wudu (ablution) and repeats.” He said: “And if it is not flowing, he performs wudu (ablution) and continues from where he left off.” He said: “And that is done between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.”
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The meaning of his saying عليه السلام, “he performs wudu (ablution),” is that he washes the place, as we explained previously.

key_terms.بَنَى: he continues from where he left off without starting over
key_terms.بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَ الْمَرْوَةِ: during the rite of movement between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah in hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.دَمٌ سَائِلٌ: flowing blood that affects the ruling more strictly
key_terms.يَتَوَضَّأُ: here explained as washing the affected area rather than performing full ritual wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: he repeats the act he was performing

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if flowing or non-flowing blood appears during worship or saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning blood encountered during ritual activity. If the blood is flowing, the act must be repeated, while if it is not flowing, the person cleanses himself and continues. The compiler then clarifies that “wudu (ablution)” here means washing the affected area, not a full ritual wudu.
